entities.name: Q17 — The Compass of an Unbuilt Ship

value.summary: Hook: Tavaros returns a salt-worn compass engraved with the name of a ship scheduled to be built next year. Layers: prophecy → reused metal and future procurement fraud → the compass also reacts to one older Concord route no modern chart records. Objectives: 1. Authenticate materials, engraving sequence, wear, and ownership. 2. Determine how the future ship name entered the object and why Tavaros returned it now. 3. Follow or secure the hidden route without surrendering the compass to one claimant. Routes: craft analysis, dock records, question dragon witnesses, sea trial, future contract investigation, historical chart comparison, or controlled duplicate. Clues: engraving newer than wear; brass from a decommissioned ship; Pella's mentor's tool marks; needle deviation near a sealed Hall key; future contract secretly pre-awarded. Failure forward: a claimant seizes the compass, but copies, craft evidence, and Tavaros's route remain. Aftermath: the procurement fraud…

Hook: Missing League Chair Ansel Daro left three authentic resignation letters, each naming a different reason, successor, and place of refuge. Layers: indecisive politician → deliberate contingency against three anticipated kidnappers → a fourth actor helped Ansel escape all of them. Objectives: 1. Determine intended recipient and trigger for each letter. 2. Locate Ansel or establish voluntary safe contact. 3. Prevent factions from using contradictory letters to seize League process. Routes: handwriting and seal analysis, courier interviews, public procedural challenge, follow three false trails, decode grocery list, protect secret refuge, or stage a fourth resignation. Clues: different paper watermarks; one impossible seasonal fruit; punctuation as harbour basin numbers; dry-sock payment; Ansel's known habit of writing contingency apologies. Riddle: “I leave by three doors and remain in the room. Which resignation is mine?” The answer is the office, not Ansel:…

entities.name: Q19 — The Flowers Inside the Sealed Hall

value.summary: Hook: Fresh flowers appear weekly inside the Concord hall sealed since Year 1 AS. Layers: ghostly remembrance → hidden maintenance route and civic ritual → Council of Margins uses the same route to inspect archive seals. Objectives: 1. Observe or enter the Hall without damaging records or creating a public crush. 2. Identify the flower bearer, maintenance route, and separate later intruders. 3. Decide immediate custody and access while preserving evidence of Council activity. Routes: stakeout, architecture, old workers' families, roof access, drainage tunnel, ritual participation, legal petition, or magical sensing. Clues: two kinds of mud; flowers from Brokers' Orchard; old municipal invoices; wax flecks under archive door; bearer is an elderly cleaner preserving a private memorial, not the spy. Failure forward: public attention forces the Hall open under poor conditions, increasing political actors but also transparency. Aftermath: archive evidence connects Cel…

entities.name: Q20 — The Village That Is Not There

value.summary: Hook: The party follows saffron to a populated Namar village absent from tax rolls, maps, and royal service lists. Layers: smuggler settlement → community erased long ago for protection → current brokers exploit legal invisibility and Sable Annek collects erased names. Objectives: 1. Earn community consent and understand benefits and harms of invisibility. 2. Trace current grain, tax, service, and identity exploitation. 3. Pursue recognition, protected status, continued secrecy, or another negotiated form chosen with residents. Routes: puppet performance, canal work, legal research, broker infiltration, royal petition, mutual-aid records, secret census controlled by residents, or confronting collectors. Clues: songs list villages; dry-sock accounts; cargo weights; old purge order; black-scale tokens; families with births but no legal deaths. Failure forward: officials discover the place before protection is ready, creating an urgent defence and negotiation rather…

entities.name: Q21 — Seed for the Wrong Season

value.summary: Hook: Namar granaries contain short-lived seed while durable flood-resistant stock appears in foreign warehouses. Layers: theft by hungry farmers → substitution inside royal distribution → export network backed by officials and investors betting on next year's shortage. Objectives: 1. Test seed, storage conditions, and distribution records before planting. 2. Identify substitution points and protect whistleblowers. 3. Restore enough viable stock while choosing how to expose or disrupt the market scheme. Routes: agricultural expertise, warehouse tracking, controlled purchase, canal interception, public germination test, negotiation with Seed Mothers, or alternate stock exchange. Clues: husk colour, storage dust, three resignation-letter grocery list, export seals, missing barge time, one broker's unusually accurate weather insurance. Failure forward: part of the crop fails, creating relief and political consequences but also clear proof. Aftermath: a copper paymen…

Layers: warehouse theft → ambitious Keeper using forged authority → foreign effort to wake Karsh and disrupt copper markets → real dragon bargain misunderstood by all sides. Objectives: 1. Trace copper from assay through storage, caravan, and mountain delivery. 2. Expose authorization fraud and the investors behind it. 3. Prevent, renegotiate, fulfil, or end the dangerous tithe process with informed Kethrian consent. Routes: account audit, mine infiltration, caravan protection, forge-mark comparison, council hearing, mountain ascent, dragon parley, decoy tithe, or exposing pact history. Clues: copied signature but wrong courtesy formula; warm canal; embercats; doubled foreign copper futures; old tithe objects include written climate records Karsh values. Hook: Tessaran astronomers predict a harmless comet while three factions claim it validates incompatible political prophecies. Layers: prophecy fraud → sincere cultural interpretations exploited by court → one observation really is impossible because an object moves against the comet. Objectives: 1. Protect observers, instruments, and public access during the comet's approach. 2. Separate measurement, interpretation, forgery, and political use. 3. Investigate the impossible companion observation without feeding harmful panic. Routes: observation, instrument checking, public teaching, debate, performance satire, guard work, court negotiation, magical study, or following the moving object. Clues: altered lens mount; playwright source for one prophecy; consistent measurements from rival schools; glass-locust flight; an object blinking in old Lantern signal intervals. Hook: The Aur exposes Old Aur Island foundations and three valid courts claim land, water, treasure, and burial authority. Layers: treasure dispute → pre-Concord community and diverted river evidence → current estates depend on historic flooding others never consented to. Objectives: 1. Stabilize the site and protect burials, navigation, and nearby households. 2. establish layers of use, alteration, and claim through material and living evidence. 3. reach a provisional arrangement before the next flood changes the site again. Routes: archaeology, river engineering, legal hearing, community assembly, controlled salvage, oral history, magical sensing, or reburial agreement. Clues: water wear, River Throne script, Concord survey cuts, family stories, fish traps, and an estate wall aligned to the redirected channel. Failure forward: flood removes some evidence but reveals another area and forces shared emergency work. Aftermath: a recovered pre-Concord tablet contrad…

Hook: Black-scale tokens and preserved archive debris lead into Sable Annek's brackish domain. Layers: monster lair → dragon archive of erased names → Annek protects some people and exploits others by controlling legal absence. Objectives: 1. Reach the basin and establish safe terms or viable escape routes. 2. identify which names, records, and living communities Annek controls. 3. recover, copy, bargain for, destroy, or redistribute evidence without exposing everyone blindly. Routes: stealth, parley, legal exchange, archive expertise, environmental diversion, community representatives, dragon leverage, or combat if supported and chosen. Clues: purchased names; preserved purge orders; brokers' contracts; genuine asylum records; Annek's hatred of the Seventh Ledger's standardized ownership. Failure forward: Annek retains records or expels the party but reveals enough to challenge the Council and may pursue later bargains. Aftermath: one recovered name belongs to a…

Hook: Evidence identifies a Council meeting distributed across several synchronized archive rooms rather than one fortress. Layers: secret ruling cabal → divided custodians, restorationists, and reformers → no member has complete control, and several believe they prevent worse state capture. Objectives: 1. Map Council membership, communication, factions, and current restoration actions. 2. interrupt coercive operations without destroying all cross-border coordination blindly. 3. expose, fracture, negotiate, replace, or reform the Council through allies earned across Caldris. Routes: infiltration, public evidence, cell defections, simultaneous hearings, courier network, archive occupation, political congress, or targeted confrontation. Clues: differing margin marks; Ansel's letters; Celyn's policies; Dry Sock accounts; community archives; authentic Ilyr mark used without current consent. entities.name: Q27 — The Archive That Answers Back

value.summary: Hook: Ilyr's Listening Caves echo visitors' words with contradictory historical testimony. Layers: dragon treasure vault → archive designed to resist single narratives → Ilyr's selective custody is itself a form of power. Objectives: 1. navigate the caves while preserving group memory, safety, and consent. 2. obtain corroborated testimony about the Concord, Council, and dragon's role. 3. persuade, compel, bargain with, expose, rob, or oppose Ilyr regarding archive custody. Routes: riddles, testimony comparison, respectful parley, stealth, public delegation, copy teams, legal/moral argument, dragon combat only if supported and unavoidable. Clues: echoes disagree consistently by witness position; missing testimonies leave salt patterns; Ilyr's early advice; letters proving withdrawal; communities requesting records and receiving jokes. Riddle: “What belongs to you, is spoken by others, changes when written, and dies when only one keeper remains?” Acceptable answers…

Layers: hidden rightful heir → law permits several legitimate structures → Vane's emergency system could decide the outcome by controlling roads and messages. Objectives: 1. keep communication, essential government, and public safety functioning without silent seizure. 2. surface legitimate claims, stakeholder rights, and manipulated procedures. 3. support a peaceful provisional settlement that remains revisable through lawful consent. Routes: council facilitation, message security, public assembly, heir investigation, Veyr and Ordelain precedents, direct protection, exposing forged proclamations, or convincing Vane to limit her own office. Layers: diplomatic summit → each delegation brings a valid local fear → actors try to package unrelated crises into one enforceable settlement. Objectives: 1. keep delegates, witnesses, couriers, and public access functioning through pressure and sabotage. 2. prevent one bloc from controlling evidence, procedure, or emergency powers. 3. help produce, reject, split, or replace an accord whose consequences are intelligible. Hook: With conspirators exposed and archives opened, ordinary disputes still require records, standards, routes, and enforcement. Destroying the old system is easier than replacing its useful functions. Layers: final boss victory → institutional vacuum → the campaign's true conclusion is how power, memory, and correction are distributed. Objectives: 1. identify essential services, vulnerable people, dangerous powers, and trustworthy local owners. 2. establish a bounded transition for records, standards, roads, debts, privacy, and correction. 3. return to affected communities and accept the visible costs and benefits of the chosen settlement. Routes: distributed archives, independent standards guild, reformed Council, public copies with privacy rules, royal compact, community custody, dragon testimony, deliberate plural systems, or another evidence-backed design. entities.name: Q31 — The Ford That Grew Too Deep

value.summary: Thread: Hearth with an optional Deep-history door. Hook: Sourapple Ford's autumn cattle drove arrives to find the crossing chest-deep, while the upstream mill insists its repaired weir changed nothing. Layers: blocked livestock road → competing water needs and an inaccurate repair survey → face-down Concord stones beneath the old ford reveal someone redirected the channel decades ago. Objectives: 1. Keep the herd, travelers, and downstream gardens safe while the crossing is unusable. 2. Establish what changed the water and which users have legitimate immediate needs. 3. Secure a workable crossing or water agreement before weather traps the drove. Approaches and clues: Hesta reads reeds and anxious cattle; Nessa can compare ferry depth; mill timbers show several generations of alteration; diving, temporary rope lanes, an upstream bypass, court mediation, or coordinated gate timing can all work. entities.name: Q32 — The Hills Keep Their Buttons

value.summary: Thread: Deep history; independent of the Measure conspiracy. Hook: A sinkhole swallows a shepherd's hut during steady rain, revealing shelves, sealed jars, and hundreds of sorted buttons beneath a supposedly ancient tomb. Layers: rescue in unstable chalk → pre-kingdom famine storehouse → a modern land claimant has been removing seals to support an exclusive ancestral story. Objectives: 1. Rescue anyone trapped and prevent a wider collapse around the opened chamber. 2. Determine the site's practical purpose without destroying its fragile evidence. 3. Decide how access, recovered supplies, and public interpretation should be shared. Approaches and clues: Linnet's survey diagrams, children's button collections, airflow through adjacent chambers, jar residue, nonhuman chew marks, and several burial traditions provide distinct routes. The old inventory puzzle sorts objects by “what closes, what carries, what remembers”; a button, jar lid, and marked tally belong toget…
